events.title: Lord Nguyen Hoang entered to defend Thuan Hoa
events.description: Nguyen Hoang, along with his family and soldiers, stationed in Ai Tu, starting the career of the Nguyen lords in Dang Trong. The land of Ai Tu - Tra Bat became the first capital, laying the foundation for the southward expansion of the territory.

events.title: Issuing the Can Vuong Edict at Tan So
events.description: After the fall of the Hue Citadel, Ton That Thuyet took King Ham Nghi to the Tan So base. Here, on behalf of the king, he issued the first Can Vuong Edict, calling on scholars, intellectuals, and the people to rise up and help the king save the country.

events.title: Establishment of the Communist Party Committee of Quang Tri Province
events.description: At the house of Mrs. Nguyen Thi Loi (Phuoc Kiem Village), the Conference to establish the Quang Tri Province Party Committee was held, electing a provisional Executive Committee. This was a milestone marking the direct leadership of the Party over the local revolutionary movement.

events.title: The 17th Parallel and the division of the country
events.description: According to the Geneva Accords, the Ben Hai River (17th parallel) was chosen as the temporary military demarcation line. Hien Luong Bridge became a symbol of the pain of division between the North and the South for over 20 years.

events.title: Airstrikes on Con Co Island
events.description: The US Air Force and Navy began fiercely attacking Con Co Island - the 'outpost watchtower' of the socialist North. The officers and soldiers of Con Co Island fought resiliently for many years, receiving commendation letters from Uncle Ho 3 times.

events.title: Completion of Vinh Moc Tunnels
events.description: The military and people of Vinh Linh painstakingly dug the Vinh Moc tunnel system, nearly 2km long in the red basalt soil, to serve as a shelter and living space for hundreds of residents against the destructive bombing of the US military.

events.title: Route 9 - Khe Sanh Campaign
events.description: The People's Army of Vietnam launched a campaign to besiege the US Marine base at Khe Sanh (Ta Con). The 77-day siege attracted and pinned down a large force of US troops, creating favorable conditions for the Tet Offensive across the South.

events.title: First liberation of Quang Tri Town
events.description: During the 1972 Strategic Offensive, our troops breached the Route 9 defense line, forcing the Saigon army to retreat. Quang Tri Province was liberated for the first time, sending shockwaves through international public opinion.

events.title: The 81-day-and-night battle to defend the Ancient Citadel
events.description: The US and ARVN military launched an operation to reoccupy Quang Tri. The Liberation Army soldiers held their ground resiliently in the Quang Tri Ancient Citadel for 81 days and nights (from June 28 to September 16) under an unprecedentedly horrific density of bombs and shells, writing an immortal epic.

events.title: Inauguration of the Headquarters of the Provisional Revolutionary Government
events.description: After the Paris Peace Accords were signed, the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam established its headquarters in Cam Lo. Here, many foreign ambassadors came to present their credentials, notably the historic visit of Cuban President Fidel Castro (September 1973).

events.title: Re-establishment of Quang Tri Province
events.description: The 8th National Assembly passed a Resolution to split Binh Tri Thien Province (merged since 1976) back into 3 provinces: Quang Binh, Quang Tri, and Thua Thien Hue. Quang Tri Province officially resumed operations on July 1, 1989.
